Can you come to a hospital room in Charlotte today?

Yes. Same-day and 24/7 emergency bedside notarization is the core of what I do. Call or text me with the hospital and how many signatures are needed, and I come to the room — often within hours, once nursing staff clears the visit.

How fast can an emergency notary arrive?

It depends on your location and the time of day, but same-day is the norm and I can often reach a Charlotte-area hospital or home within a couple of hours. For overnight and holiday requests, calling reaches me fastest.

What if the patient does not have a physical ID?

If a driver's license or passport was left at home, North Carolina law (G.S. 10B-3) may allow the use of one or two credible identifying witnesses instead. Call me to describe the situation and I will confirm whether that option is legally viable before I arrive.

Can you notarize for someone who is sedated or in the ICU?

Only if the signer is alert enough to understand the document and is signing willingly. By law I must confirm awareness and free will, so I cannot notarize for a patient who is unconscious or too heavily medicated to communicate.

What emergency documents do you notarize?

The urgent ones families need most: a durable or healthcare power of attorney before surgery, an advance directive or living will during an admission, hospice and HIPAA paperwork, and last-minute estate or real estate documents.

Which Charlotte hospitals and facilities do you cover?

The major Atrium Health and Novant Health hospitals, plus hospice, nursing homes, and assisted living facilities across Mecklenburg, Cabarrus, and Union counties — bedside, at home, or wherever the signer is.

Where I go

Emergency and same-day service throughout Charlotte and the surrounding metro. For facility-specific detail, see my hospital & bedside notary, nursing home notary, and after-hours notary pages.

A note on what I can and can't do

I am a commissioned North Carolina Notary Public, not an attorney. I verify identity, confirm the signer is aware and willing, and witness the signature — I cannot draft documents or give legal advice. For the wording or legal effect of a document, consult a licensed North Carolina attorney.
